Setting ("The year is 2281. Roughly 200 years ago the USA and China were locked in a prolonged war over a depleting stock of natural resources, leading to a nuclear armageddon. The world was reduced to an uninhabitable hellhole, but US citizen were spared the fate of extinction that befell the rest of the world by hiding in underground fallout bunkers called "Vaults" provided by Vault-Tec. Most of these Vaults were dedicated to some manner of social experiment that would usually end in catastrophe, but some were legitimate shelters against the nukes. Eventually, the residents of the Vaults, also known as Vault Dwellers, ventured topside and began to re-establish life on the surface once the background radiation became tolerable. But not all life on the surface was wiped out, many flora and fauna had mutated, whether it be naturally or due the meddling of human hands via the FEV, short for Forced Evolutionary Virus. Such as Deathclaws, mutated from the Jackson's chameleon, but seldom resemble them, appearing more as bipedal devils than anything else. Now, a war for territory and control wages between two sides over the Mojave Desert. From the west. the ever expanding, militaristic and imperialist New California Republic, NCR for short, seeking to bring back the old fashioned US democracy back into the new world. From the east, the ruthless and merciless Ceasar's Legion, aiming to bring a world of strength divorced from the reliance on technology, styled after the Roman Empire. And between these two sides lies a third player, the enigmatic Mr. House, the founder and owner of Rob Co. a company renowned for it's revolutionary robotics, has survived into the post-apocalyptic age. Responsible for saving and preserving the New Vegas strip, ruling over it with a hands off approach. Though not a participant in the conflict between the NCR and The Legion, he is friend to neither. Mojave locals aren't fond of the NCR nor The Legion coming onto their turf. Due to the decline of the NCR's gold reserves, their paper currency has lost much of it's value, the Mojave's denizens instead prioritizing bottlecaps as a currency, as they are backed by the Water Merchants, and thus have value due to the bottlecaps associated with the Merchant's water bottles. Although frowned upon, gold coins minted by The Legion are more valuable due to the inherent value of gold. Brahmin, Brahmin are the mutated descendant of cows in the wasteland, their once white fur coat with black spots gone, now replaced with bare red skin. In addition, Brahmin also sprout two heads. Despite these differences, Brahmin, are treated much the same as cattle and pack mules. Brahmin milk is a filling substance and has radiation cleansing properties. Vault 34, Vault 34 is a Vault packed with an abundance of firearms, explosives and etc. Vault 34's residents eventually left, along with their weaponry and took over Nellis Air Force Base as their home, renaming themselves "The Boomers", hurling artillery shells at anyone who would come near their home, deeming all others "savages". Not all wastelanders found a meaningful and productive existence, some take to the way of murder and robbery. Gangs of roaming criminals who prey upon others in a parasitic lifestyle, referred to as Raiders. Vault Jumpsuits, Vault Jumpsuits are full body skintight latex blue jumpsuits with yellow accents, usually adorned with the number of the Vault they belong to, worn by all Vault Dwellers. Pip-Boy, Pip-Boys are a wrist mounted PDA given to all Vault Dwellers.")
